label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Sizwe, breathe. Mechanic here, I run a workshop in Umbilo. You're not the first and you won't be the last. One customer of mine did this twice in the same year at the same garage, so we made him a sticker for the fuel flap. And in 1995, my first year as an apprentice, I put diesel in my boss's Golf. He still tells it at every braai.

Now the serious part. Take the key out and do NOT crank it again. Every time that engine turns, the pump is running on petrol with no lubrication. That's what does the damage.

Don't put diesel on top, now or later. Kobus means well, but that's old Land Rover advice and a modern common rail can't take it. The petrol is still in there and mixing does nothing.

Is it finished? Not necessarily, but I won't lie to you. It ran 3km, stalled and got cranked five or six times, so damage to the pump and injectors is possible. Nobody can tell you from a forum. It must be towed, not driven, and the pump and injectors checked first.

If they're fine, it's a tank drain, line flush, new fuel filter and a bleed, usually R2 500 to R4 500. Tash's R40 000 is what it looks like when the injection system is gone. I can't promise you a total tonight, but don't assume the worst yet.

So tonight:

1. Key out, hands off.
2. Check your insurance before you pay a tow guy cash. Most policies include a roadside tow.
3. If you want, send it to me in Umbilo. We're open tomorrow 7 till 12 and my guy Thabo can drain it first thing.

Then borrow a bakkie for the cake and the sound system anyway. Even if all goes well, don't plan your wedding around a drained tank. Start phoning now.

Congrats on the wedding, boet. In a few years this is your braai story. Just don't touch that key.
